classification.difficultyReason: Distinguish inclusive overlaps from pairwise-only regions and combine the language totals with the number inside the union to recover the target region before finding its probability.

content.prompt:
[Three-way Venn diagrams]

A class of 28 students is surveyed about what language they are able to speak, and the following results are found.

Five people could speak French, Italian and German. Two people speak none of those languages. 18 people speak French, 16 people speak Italian, 9 people speak French and German, and 14 people speak German. Two people speak Italian and German, but not French. Find the probability that a randomly selected person speaks French and Italian, but not German.

inlines.text: The French–Italian overlap outside the German circle contains 6 of the 28 students.

answer.worked:
Let $F$, $I$ and $G$ represent the students who speak French, Italian and German respectively. Let $x$ be the number in the French–Italian overlap outside $G$.

The centre contains 5 students. The French–German overlap outside $I$ contains $9-5=4$ students. The Italian–German overlap outside $F$ contains 2 students.

$$\begin{align*}\text{German only}&=14-5-4-2\\\text{German only}&=3\end{align*}$$

The French-only region contains $18-5-4-x=9-x$ students. The Italian-only region contains $16-5-2-x=9-x$ students. The seven regions inside the circles contain $28-2=26$ students in total, so $32-x=26$.

$$\begin{align*}x&=32-26\\x&=6\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}P(F\cap I\cap G^{\mathrm c})&=\frac{6}{28}\\P(F\cap I\cap G^{\mathrm c})&=\frac{3}{14}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Completed three-set Venn diagram constructed from the survey givens.
spec.mathematics: F only 3, I only 3, G only 3, F and I only 6, F and G only 4, I and G only 2, all three 5, none 2.
